prompt.context:
It's Monday morning and as a new Principal/Engagement Leader, you've just gotten a call from a well-known and respected French-based Consumer Products company. The company has offices in the US and has been selling through traditional channels throughout its history. It designs and manufactures plastic products like pens, pencils, disposable razors, etc. It's an old company that's been around for about 60 years and wants to take advantage of the Internet, starting with US sales.

You talked at length with the President of the dot-com part of the company and learned:
- The company now wants to sell directly to consumers through their Internet site.
- Their current online business is nothing more than a small catalog and is not doing very well: sales and hits are less than expected.
- It offers more convenience than their other channels (open 24x7, more product information), but limited selection — only high margin items.
- The President's strategy is to add key functionality to the online business to increase hit rate and improve revenue.
- She reports directly to the CEO.
- She wants your consulting team to create: (1) a multi-ship-to functionality, (2) a site-wide search functionality, and (3) an ability to add checkout sales (e.g., impulse-buy items similar to end caps in grocery stores).
- She wants your consulting team to build this immediately.

This coming Thursday, you will meet with the President and her team. Her expectation is that you will present a plan for your consulting team to build the requested functionality ASAP.
prompt.question: What will you do on Monday? What will you prepare? What questions will you ask the President? What is your goal for that meeting?

framework: Recognize that accepting the client's request at face value would be a mistake — the three requested features (multi-ship-to, site-wide search, checkout impulse buys) will not materially improve hit rate or revenue based on available information
Goal for Thursday's meeting: use the presentation of a 'plan to deliver functionality' as a vehicle to gather more information and open the President's eyes to the deeper business problem
Monday prep: structure a diagnostic framework around the online store's value proposition to guide questioning at the meeting
Questioning logic path: target customer → value to customer → uniqueness of offering → how the online store delivers on its promise

questions.prompt: What will you do on Monday to prepare for Thursday's meeting?
questions.guidance: The candidate should plan to: (1) avoid immediately scoping a build plan, (2) research the company's products and existing channels, (3) prepare a structured set of diagnostic questions about the online business's goals and value proposition, (4) frame the meeting agenda as collaborative discovery rather than pure project scoping. The key insight is NOT to accept the client's feature requests at face value.

questions.prompt: What questions will you ask the President at Thursday's meeting?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates will probe the value proposition of the online store along a logical path: (1) Who is the store trying to target — what customer segment? (2) What is the store's real value to the customer (convenience, price, selection, or something else)? (3) Why is the online offering unique and attractive versus buying through traditional channels or competitors? (4) How will the online store actually deliver on that promise? These questions reveal whether the three requested features actually address the root problem.

questions.prompt: What is your goal for the Thursday meeting?
questions.guidance: The goal is NOT simply to present a build plan. The goal is to create a conversation with the President and her team to: (1) present a notional plan (showing responsiveness), (2) gather additional information to better understand the online business's issues and goals, (3) introduce the idea that the requested functionality may not solve the pressing underlying problem — i.e., open the President's eyes through questioning rather than confrontation.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the possible root causes why the online business has lower-than-expected sales and hit rates?

categories.name: Value Proposition Issues
ideas: Limited selection (only high-margin items) fails to meet customer expectations
No compelling reason to buy online vs. retail channels
Price may not be competitive online

categories.name: Discovery & Traffic
ideas: Low brand awareness of the online store
No digital marketing or acquisition funnel

categories.name: Site Experience
ideas: Poor navigation or product findability (hence the search request)
No upsell or cross-sell mechanism (hence the impulse-buy request)
Site design not optimized for conversion

categories.name: Fulfillment & Trust
ideas: Shipping costs or lead times unattractive vs. retail
Lack of consumer trust in direct-brand e-commerce

categories.name: Strategic Misalignment
ideas: Online channel conflicts with retail partners (channel conflict)
Internal org not structured to support DTC e-commerce
President's KPIs (hits vs. revenue) may be misaligned

recommendation: Do not immediately commit to building the three requested features; instead, reframe the Thursday meeting as a diagnostic session to establish the true value proposition of the online store before prescribing solutions
Recommend a short discovery phase (1-2 weeks) to assess target customer, competitive positioning, and root causes of low traffic and conversion before investing in feature development
risks: President may resist having her feature requests questioned — manage by framing diagnostics as ensuring the build investment succeeds
Discovery phase adds delay, which may frustrate the CEO's urgency; mitigate by showing a fast-track timeline
Channel conflict with traditional retail partners has not been addressed and may constrain online strategy
next_steps: Monday: prepare diagnostic question framework around value proposition (Who / What / Why / How)
Thursday meeting: present notional build timeline but use it as context to open diagnostic conversation; secure agreement on a brief discovery sprint
Post-meeting: document findings and align on whether features should be built, modified, or deprioritized in light of root-cause diagnosis
